title: What is a Data Structure, and What is an Algorithm?
excerpt: A data structure organizes data so the operations you need are cheap. An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps. Together they determine whether your solution runs in milliseconds or minutes.
author: BountyCode Team
body:
## The short answer

A **data structure** organizes data so the operations you need are cheap: an array reads by index in O(1), a hash table finds a key in O(1) on average. An **algorithm** is a finite sequence of steps from input to output, such as binary search.

You choose them together: finding duplicates pair by pair is O(n²); with a hash set it is O(n).

## Why it matters in interviews

Interviewers don't care that you memorized a definition. They care that you can say, out loud, "we mostly look up by key, so a hash map" before writing code.
